title: Anthropic's Claude Science creates the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky
key_facts: Anthropic's Claude Science mapped the whole sky in ultraviolet light, described as a first.
Johns Hopkins astrophysicist Brice Menard describes the process on Anthropic's website.
UV can only be measured from space because the ozone layer blocks it; NASA's GALEX covered about two-thirds of the sky and skipped bright star-forming regions.
Claude Science coordinated AI agents that downloaded data from several space missions, calibrated and merged it.
Missing areas were filled by inpainting, where a model learns from existing data to reconstruct gaps.
In tests, predictions averaged about ten percent deviation from actual measurements.
The map is meant as teaching material; Menard suspects many scientists have put off similar projects AI could now make possible.
